primaryText: Mary is feeling sick then.
comment: In a root clause the perspective is the utterance time, which the present overlaps and *then* must avoid; the past and future of (7) admit *then*. The row expands the starred variant of the printed (6) Mary is feeling sick (*then).

primaryText: Mary was feeling sick then.
comment: The past denotes a time apart from the utterance time, which *then* can restrict. The row expands the printed (7a) Mary was feeling sick (then).

primaryText: Mary will be feeling sick then.
comment: The future denotes a time apart from the utterance time, which *then* can restrict. The row expands the printed (7b) Mary will be feeling sick (then).

primaryText: To 2000, o Yanis iksere oti i Maria ine egkios.
translation: In 2000, Yanis knew that Maria was (lit. is) pregnant.

readings.name: shifted present: the pregnancy overlaps the knowledge in 2000

comment: The 2000, det Yanis know.PAST that the Maria be.PRES pregnant: the embedded present refers to a past time overlapping the matrix attitude, tense shift.

primaryText: To 2000, o Yanis iksere oti i Maria ine egkios tote.
translation: In 2000, Yanis knew that Maria was (lit. is) pregnant then.
comment: The ⌜then⌝-present puzzle: the shifted present does not refer to the utterance time, yet *tote* remains incompatible with it; from Tsilia (2021). The row expands the starred variant of the printed (*tote).

primaryText: Lifney alpayim šana, Yosef xašav še Miriam ohevet oto az.
translation: 2,000 years ago, Yosef thought that Miriam loved (lit. loves) him then.
comment: Before 2,000 year, Yosef think.PAST that Miriam love.PRES him then; from Ogihara and Sharvit (2012), who note that not all speakers reject it. The row expands the starred variant of the printed (*az).

primaryText: V 2016 godu Tanja skazala, čto Putin togda ∅ prezident Rossii.
translation: In 2016 Tanja said that Putin was (lit. is) the president of Russia then.
comment: in 2016 year Tanja say.PAST that Putin then be.PRES president.NOM Russia.GEN; from Vostrikova (2019). The row expands the starred variant of the printed (*togda).

primaryText: A month ago, John found out that Mary loves him.

readings.name: double access: Mary loves John at the utterance time and at the finding out

comment: The English present under past never shifts: it indicates the utterance time, and (19) with *two thousand years ago* is infelicitous; *then* is impossible, (20).

primaryText: A month ago, John found out that Mary loves him then.
comment: The unshifted English present of (18) overlaps the utterance time, so *then* is impossible with it.

primaryText: In his childhood, Joseph met a woman who loves traveling then.
Prin 20 chronia o Pavlos sinerghastike me enan andra pu ine proedros tote.
translation: 20 years ago, Pavlos collaborated with a man who is president (now).
comment: Greek, Hebrew, (26), and Russian, (27), do not shift the present in relative clauses under past, an extensional environment with no operator to bind the index. The row expands the starred variant of the printed (*tote); the translation is the printed reading of the sentence without it.

primaryText: ninenn mae, Yusuke-wa Yukiko-ga tooji ninnshinn shite-iru to shitteita.
translation: 2 years ago, Yusuke knew that Yukiko was (lit. is) pregnant.
comment: 2-years before Yusuke-TOP Yukiko-NOM then pregnant be-PRES with know.PAST: Japanese shifts the present under past in attitude reports and, uniquely, in relative clauses, (29), and the puzzle arises in both. The row expands the starred variant of the printed (*tooji); the printed translation has no then.

primaryText: ninenn mae, Yusuke-wa tooji seifu de hatarai-te-iru hito to renkei o hakat-te-ita.
translation: Two years ago, Yusuke collaborated with a man who was (lit. is) president.
comment: The row expands the starred variant of the printed (*tooji); the printed translation has no then.

primaryText: To 2030, i Maria tha pi oti ine sti filaki tote.
translation: In 2030, Maria will say that she is in jail (in 2030).
comment: Under future almost every surveyed language shifts the present, in attitude reports and relative clauses alike, since WOLL binds an index; Greek, Hebrew, (30b), and Russian, (30c), show the puzzle there too. The row expands the starred variant of the printed (*tote); the printed translation has no then.

primaryText: In 2030, John will say that he is in jail then.
comment: English tolerates *then* with the present under future, for some speakers here and generally in relative clauses, (31d): the present is deleted by sequence of tense under WOLL's PRES rather than shifted, (92)–(93). The page prints (%then): % marks variation among speakers, "at least for some speakers".

primaryText: To 2030, i Zoi tha ine pantremeni me kapion pu ine tote sti filaki.
translation: In 2030, Zoe will be married to someone who is in jail.
comment: The row expands the starred variant of the printed (*tote); the printed translation has no then.

primaryText: In 2030, John will be married to someone who is in jail then.
comment: The present under future is deleted by sequence of tense under WOLL's PRES, (91), (93), and a deleted tense carries no perspectival presupposition. From Tsilia (2021), adapted from von Fintel and Heim; the row expands the printed (then).

primaryText: Tooji ai-mashou.
context: Two friends are making plans to go to the movies on Saturday; one says this before they leave.
comment: Japanese *tooji* is used only with past expressions, so it is ruled out even with a matrix future tense, and the present-under-future cells are not applicable for Japanese.

primaryText: lifney alpayim šana, Yosef xašav še Miriam ahava oto az.
translation: Two thousand years ago Yosef believed that Miriam loved him then.

readings.name: simultaneous: the love overlaps the belief

comment: An embedded past with the same simultaneous reference as the shifted present admits *az*, so the puzzle is not a restriction on the reference; Russian (39) likewise.

primaryText: A week ago, John said that in ten days he would say to his girlfriend that they were meeting then for the last time.

readings.name: the meeting is at the time of the future saying, three days from now

comment: The most deeply embedded past is past relative to no time in the sentence, so it is deleted; deleted tense carries no perspectival presupposition and *then* is compatible with it, (89a); Greek (49) likewise.

primaryText: To 1960, o Yanis iksere oti i Maria ine omorfi tora.
translation: In 1960, Yanis knew that Maria was (lit. is) beautiful.
comment: The present shifts but *tora* 'now' does not, and Hebrew *axšav* likewise, (100): the perspective is not the context's time. The row expands the variant of the printed (#tora); the printed translation has no now.
